A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MMVU study with complete main text and supplementary material. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original MMVU evaluations, fine-tuning and prompting experiments, attention analyses, and extensive supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: The paired-data construction pipeline, CGR, and VAR, including Algorithm 1, remain unchanged. The added weight-merging statement documents the existing experiment without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 12-category MMVU benchmark, 1,786 questions, MMVU-Train, and the same supplementary training datasets and general evaluation benchmarks. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and supplementary experiments, including the 15 MLLMs in Table 1 and instruction-dataset comparisons in Table 3. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The benchmark subsets, metrics, training configurations, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 4.3 newly mentions weight merging but does not revise a previously stated setting or establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The prompting, image-input, negative-sample, conversation-round, question-type, and dataset-mixture analyses are retained. Supplementary sections C and D become sections 8 and 9 without adding or removing analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. Model-confidence and attention analyses remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and supplementary Tables 1–13, renumbered 5–17 in v3, retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports the same 63.49 RA and 21.03 MR for LLaVA-OneVision-7B + MMVU-Train. Graphs and qualitative examples also retain their findings.

T1.justification: The MR and RA formulas, attention calculations, logit normalization, and Algorithm 1 mathematics are unchanged. Section 3.3 expands explanations of the existing UR, UF, NR, and NF categories without changing their mathematical meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: misresponses despite visual understanding, the MMVU benchmark and paired training data, and mitigation through CGR and VAR.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 modestly qualifies its interpretation, changing paired data 'significantly reduces biased responses' to 'can reduce biased responses.' The mechanism explanations and supplementary limitation concerning dataset-construction cost remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly discloses weight merging for the Section 4.3 experiment and supplies a project repository link where v2 only promised future release. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or availability. Appendix prompts, hyperparameters, and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds five references: FineCLIPER, Beyond Uncertainty, EyeFound, VideoXL, and Intervening Anchor Token. These broaden the cited background without substantively changing the paper's novelty argument or relationship to its principal comparators.

P1.justification: v3 expands the metric-category explanations, makes limited wording and author-information edits, and extends the contents listing to the main text. Supplementary sections A–I become sections 6–14; the narrative order is retained.

P2.justification: v3 compacts main-table layouts, moves Table 2 from PDF page 6 to page 5, and adjusts captions and surrounding text placement. Supplementary figures and tables receive continuous numbering; their visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 explains the metric categories more clearly, discloses weight merging in the main experiment, and provides a concrete repository link. These modestly improve clarity and reproducibility documentation while preserving the scientific evidence. Denser main tables introduce a small readability tradeoff.
